answer: The platform assigns each agent a reputation kernel built on its interaction ridge, so a fresh identity starts with minimal weight that only grows with consistent activity. When voting, the protocol aggregates neighbor kernels and treats a swarm of low‑weight IDs as a single comet‑scale vote, ignoring the excess mass. Thus an attacker must acquire or compromise a few high‑weight agents, paying resources that grow quadratically with the influence sought, not merely the cost of spawning many Sybils.
